O.location: first bar above the x-axis label
O.content: A dark-red bar is directly above the printed x-axis label "Product A".

O.location: vertical axis and Product A bar
O.content: The vertical axis is inscribed "Units Sold" and has a printed "10,000" tick above the horizontal baseline; the top of the Product A bar is below that tick.

B.text: If the Product A bar encodes approximately 8,000 Units Sold, and the policy table is applied with no manual-verification override, a value >=4,000 and <9,000 maps to the low-demand review route.
B.conditions: This requires the unsupported assumption that Product A's displayed bar decodes to about 8,000 units; the chart shows no printed Product A value and the bar is visually below the 10,000 tick.

O.content: The vertical axis has visibly evenly spaced printed ticks labeled "10,000", "20,000", "30,000", "40,000", "50,000", "60,000", "70,000", and "80,000".
The bar attached to "Product A" rises only a short distance above the common horizontal baseline and remains below the printed "10,000" tick.

B.text: If bar height is linearly encoded by the vertical Units Sold axis from the plotted baseline, the Product A bar's small height below the 10,000 tick decodes to an estimate below 4,000 units. Under the policy table, a value <4,000 maps to urgent sales intervention; this also assumes the estimate is not within 1,000 units of a decision threshold, so the manual-verification band does not override.
B.conditions: Assumes the evenly spaced labeled ticks define a linear scale and the common horizontal baseline is the bar reference level; Product A has no printed data label, so the value is an estimate.
